note: Prompts-only view of evals/ui_family_cases.json for the family A/B. No anchors, so answer arms never see the rubric. Keep prompts byte-identical to the case file.

cases.prompt: Our new invoices screen has no rows yet. What should we show instead of a blank table? Also, what should the empty-state button label be?
Every row in our projects table has 6 actions (edit, duplicate, share, archive, export, delete). All 6 as icon buttons feels noisy and wide. How should I present row-level actions?

Our dashboard shows total users over 12 months in a card, plus a second card with this month's total. I am choosing between a full line chart and a big number with a small trend indicator for the second card. Which and why?
Cards, a modal, and a dropdown on one page all use the same large shadow and read as one blob. How do I differentiate elevation so depth reads without clutter?
My order-confirmation email renders fine in Gmail but breaks in Outlook: grid columns collapse and image spacing multiplies. What is the general approach to authoring cross-client email?
A user submits a form and the server times out. Should I show a toast? The app is also half-down, so a persistent system banner exists. How do I choose between inline error, toast, and banner here?
A settings nav has 3 sections. One section holds 30 toggles and sliders; the other two have 5 fields each. Same page or tabs? And is toggles-everywhere even right?
We want a delete row with only a trash icon and a profile icon button, no text. Is icon-only acceptable? What exactly is required for it?

We have a settings page with 3 sections: account profile (5 fields), notifications (2 toggles), and permissions (2 selects). It looks thin and empty. Should I reorganize as cards, tabs, or a dashboard layout?

New users land on an empty project board. We spent a while reasoning about whether to show a checklist tour, a product-tour tooltip, or a blank-slate card. What is the better onboarding approach and when?
We display 40 deployments per environment. Customers need to scan by column (name, status, age, commit). Is a table, a card list, or a tile grid the right pattern here?
Our desktop table is 9 columns wide. Which responsive pattern is the right one for narrow phones: horizontal scroll, collapse to cards, hide columns, or a separate view?
We need a type scale for a marketing + app dashboard. We have 9 font sizes in use across screens. How do we build a sane scale from this?

A settings page has a big hero title, a prominent install banner, small form labels, and every button equally styled. Users cannot see what to do first. How do I fix the hierarchy without adding color or larger whitespace?
